situation.margin_position: The 2025 operating margin of 26.6% sits at the company's 7-year median of about 26.6%. 2026 is far above it because the US-Iran conflict and Hormuz disruption pushed freight rates to historic highs, with 9M 2026 EBIT at 45.3% of revenue and full-year EBITDA guidance of USD 1,350-1,500m. tax_rate_representative.why: The base-year tax rate of 3.1% fits the very small tax charges (9M 2026 tax of 3.0 on pretax profit of 662.8) of a shipping group, which suggests a tonnage-tax-type regime.

situation.why: 2025 was a middling year: revenue fell to 1,339.5 and net profit to 286.0. 2026 is a peak year, with 9M revenue of 1,564.2 against 986.9 a year earlier and 88% of days fixed at USD/day 50,487. growth_thesis.claim: A newbuilding pipeline is intended to extend growth. The company exercised options on two more MR newbuildings. After quarter-end it agreed eight LR2 newbuildings through a 50/50 joint venture and secured options on two more MR vessels. This needs ongoing financing and on-time deliveries; prepayments on vessels were 71.0 (table in millions) at the latest balance sheet against 14.1 (table in millions) at the prior year-end, and borrowings rose by USD 135m.
quotes: TORM exercised options for an additional two MR newbuildings.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited item (coverage table and outlook).
growth_thesis.claim: Forward coverage and guidance support near-term earnings. For the fourth quarter, 53% of earning days were covered at USD/day 78,419. For the full year, 88% were fixed at USD/day 50,487. Full-year TCE guidance was raised at the low end to USD 1,750 - 1,900m and EBITDA guidance to USD 1,350 - 1,500m. The uncovered 4,060 days leave results exposed, since USD/day 1,000 moves EBITDA by about USD 4m.
quotes: A change in freight rates of USD/day 1,000 will, all else equal, impact EBITDA by approximately USD 4m.
We have limited visibility on TCE rates that are not yet fixed with our customers.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited item (cash flow, liquidity and going-concern text).
growth_thesis.claim: Operating cash generation and liquidity fund the fleet expansion and shareholder payouts. Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 720m against USD 364m a year earlier. Liquidity was USD 799m and the tanker net loan-to-value ratio was 25.9%. A quarterly dividend of USD 1.35 per share was set at 75% of net profit excluding non-recurring items. This holds only if cash flows stay high enough to meet covenants and fund both newbuildings and distributions.
quotes: Net cash flow from operating activities for the first nine months of 2026 was USD 720m (2025, same period: USD 364m).
The distribution represents 75% of net profit excluding non-recurring items for the quarter and is consistent with the Distribution Policy.

growth_thesis.basis: Management expectation stated in the cited item; the cost increase is from its table.
growth_thesis.claim: Margin conversion depends on costs staying contained. Management expects operating costs per vessel day and administrative expenses to stay broadly in line with prior-year levels. Tanker operating expenses per day were already 7,894 (table, USD) against 7,268 (table, USD) a year earlier.
quotes: we expect operating costs per vessel day, and administrative expenses to stay broadly in line with prior-year levels

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the income statement; the interpretation is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: The growth is cyclical and rate-led, not steady. Net profit for the full prior year was $286.0 (table in millions) against $611.5 (table in millions) the year before. Rate-driven earnings can fall sharply when freight markets weaken.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited company announcement.
growth_thesis.claim: A corporate-control situation may shape the strategy. Hafnia holds about 19.8% of TORM and plans to distribute that stake to its shareholders. The TORM board says it unanimously rejected Hafnia's all-share combination proposals as substantially undervaluing the company. Continued independent growth assumes the board keeps this stance.
quotes: each of the proposals substantially undervalued TORM

material_events.basis: Stated in the company announcement (P4). The announcement is dated 18 November 2026 on its page footer.
material_events.claim: TORM's Board confirmed that it unanimously rejected Hafnia's conditional all-share combination proposals, which it said offered no effective premium for control and undervalued TORM.
quotes: The Board of TORM confirms that Hafnia made a number of conditional, all-share proposals to effect a combination between Hafnia and TORM, offering no effective premium for control.

material_events.basis: Stated in P4 (company announcement). The N3 headline text, from a press report, supports the counter point.
material_events.claim: The TORM Board noted Hafnia's announced proposal to distribute its approximately 19.8% shareholding in TORM to Hafnia's own shareholders.
quotes: regarding the proposed distribution of its approximately 19.8% shareholding in TORM to their shareholders.

material_events.basis: The source is a press report (marketscreener.com), not a company filing. The item does not print the year.
material_events.claim: A press report says Hafnia completed the acquisition of an additional minority stake in TORM.
quotes: Nov. 17 Hafnia Limited (OB:HAFNI) completed the acquisition of an additional 4.4% minority stake in TORM plc (CPSE:TRMD A).

material_events.basis: The source is a press report (avisendanmark.dk). Only a headline and an excerpt are shown, so details are not stated.
material_events.claim: A Danish press report headline says the attempted combination of TORM and Hafnia is being dropped.
quotes: Torm-sammenlægning med Hafnia-rederi droppes.

material_events.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 interim report (P2).
material_events.claim: With Q3 2026 results, TORM raised the lower end of its full-year 2026 guidance by USD 50m. This is a guidance upgrade, not a withdrawal.
quotes: TORM has raised the lower end of its full-year guidance by USD 50m.

material_events.basis: Stated in P2. The date comes from the Board's signing date of 04 November 2026.
material_events.claim: TORM's Board approved a Q3 2026 interim dividend of USD 1.35 per share, an expected total of USD 139m, payable on 02 December 2026.
quotes: Today, TORM’s Board of Directors approved an interim dividend for the third quarter of 2026 of USD 1.35 per share corresponding to an expected total dividend payment of USD 139m.

material_events.basis: Stated in P2. The exact agreement date is not given.
material_events.claim: After the end of Q3 2026, TORM entered into agreements for eight LR2 newbuildings to be held through a 50/50 joint venture and secured options for two more MR newbuildings.
quotes: Subsequent to quarter-end, TORM entered into agreements for eight LR2 newbuildings to be held through a 50/50 joint venture structure, and secured options for an additional two MR newbuildings.

risks.basis: Rate dependence is stated in P2. The direction of the risk is inferred from the 2025 and 2024 profit figures in F2.
risks.claim: Recent earnings rest on exceptionally high freight rates tied to the US-Iran conflict. Q3 return on invested capital was 26.3% against 13.8% a year earlier. In 2025 net profit was 286.0 (table in millions) against 611.5 in 2024. A fall in rates would cut earnings sharply.
quotes: reflecting the exceptionally high freight rates
The eventual normalization of Persian Gulf trade therefore does not necessarily imply an immediate normalization of the tanker market.

risks.basis: The stake size and the rejection are stated in P4. The overhang mechanism is inferred. The press items are secondary snippets.
risks.claim: Hafnia plans to distribute its approximately 19.8% TORM stake to its own shareholders after TORM's board rejected its combination proposals. This leaves control and share-overhang uncertainty. Press reports disagree on the status: one headline says the merger attempt is dropped, another says Hafnia is taking more time to decide.
quotes: the proposed distribution of its approximately 19.8% shareholding in TORM to their shareholders
the Board concluded that each of the proposals substantially undervalued TORM and therefore did not justify engagement with Hafnia

risks.basis: Liquidity, loan-to-value and stress-case statements are in P2 and P1. The rupture scenario is a hypothetical the company itself describes, not an observed event.
risks.claim: The company is financed by debt, with covenants tied to liquidity and vessel values. If rates and vessel values fell together, covenant headroom could narrow. Liquidity at 30 September 2026 was USD 798.7m and net loan-to-value was 25.9%. The company says its reverse stress case still keeps headroom.
quotes: TORM maintains sufficient headroom on liquidity and covenants throughout the going concern period.

risks.basis: The pipeline and payout are stated in P2. The risk to cash is inferred.
risks.claim: The company is committing to a large newbuilding pipeline through 2030 while paying out 75% of net profit excluding non-recurring items as dividends. This increases capital commitments and delivery exposure at a point of very strong freight rates. The size of the commitments is not in the evidence.
quotes: Collectively, these investments establish a significant pipeline of future fleet deliveries through 2030

risks.basis: The vote outcomes and the planned policy revision are stated in P6. The effect on the company is inferred.
risks.claim: Shareholder dissent on governance: the remuneration resolutions and a share buyback authority each drew more than 20% votes against at the AGM. The board is evaluating the CEO's annual bonus approach and expects to submit a revised remuneration policy at the 2027 AGM.
quotes: each received more than 20% votes against the Board's recommendation.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P4 for the 19.8% stake and the rejected proposals. The press reports in N1, N2 and N3 are snippets, so their reconciliation is inferred.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will Hafnia's approximately 19.8% stake in TORM be distributed to Hafnia's shareholders, sold, or kept? The press items point in different directions: one says a combination is dropped, one says Hafnia's decision deadline passed unresolved, and one says Hafnia acquired an additional 4.4% stake.
quotes: The Board of TORM confirms that Hafnia made a number of conditional, all-share proposals to effect a combination between Hafnia and TORM, offering no effective premium for control.

unresolved_questions.basis: Coverage and guidance are stated in P2. Whether the guidance will be met cannot be known from this evidence.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will full-year 2026 TCE land within the raised guidance of USD 1,750 - 1,900m? Q4 2026 was only 53% covered at USD/day 78,419 as of 28 October 2026, so the open days still depend on freight rates.
quotes: full-year 2026 TCE is now expected to be in the range of USD 1,750 - 1,900m

unresolved_questions.basis: Drivers and the outlook are stated in management's own commentary in P2. The path of rates is not determinable from it.
unresolved_questions.claim: How durable are the very high product tanker rates tied to the US-Iran conflict and Persian Gulf disruption? Q3 2026 fleet TCE per day was 40,102, and the company says normalization of Gulf trade may not mean immediate normalization of the tanker market.
quotes: The eventual normalization of Persian Gulf trade therefore does not necessarily imply an immediate normalization of the tanker market.

unresolved_questions.basis: The orders are stated in P2. The missing prices and financing are inferred from their absence in the excerpts, because the notes were omitted from the packet.
unresolved_questions.claim: What is the total capital commitment and funding plan for the newbuilding programme? It includes eight LR2 newbuildings in a 50/50 joint venture, additional MR newbuildings and options, and it sits alongside a Q3 dividend. The shown evidence does not give contract prices or financing terms.
quotes: Subsequent to quarter-end, TORM entered into agreements for eight LR2 newbuildings to be held through a 50/50 joint venture structure, and secured options for an additional two MR newbuildings.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P6. The final outcome is unknown.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the revised remuneration policy and governance changes resolve the shareholder dissent? The Remuneration Resolutions and the off-market buyback resolution each drew more than 20% of votes against at the 2026 AGM, and the changes are not yet defined.
quotes: Any changes will be reflected in a revised Remuneration Policy to be submitted to shareholders for approval at the 2027 AGM.

verdict_reason: expected return +35.4 points a year against the required return over 3 years
